Background and Objectives In this retrospective longitudinal study, we aimed at exploring the role of (a) MuSK-immunoglobulin G (IgG) levels, (b) predominant MuSK-IgG subclasses, and (c) antibody affinity as candidate biomarkers of severity and outcomes in MuSK-MG, using and comparing different antibody testing techniques. Methods Total MuSK-IgGs were quantified with radioimmunoassay (RIA), ELISA, flow cytometry, and cell-based assay (CBA) serial dilutions using HEK293 cells transfected with MuSK-eGFP. MuSK-IgG subclasses were measured by flow cytometry. SAffCon assay was used for determining MuSK-IgG affinity. Results Forty-three serum samples were obtained at different time points from 20 patients with MuSK-MG (median age at onset: 48 years, interquartile range = 27.5–72.5; women, 16/20), with 9 of 20 (45%) treated with rituximab. A strong correlation between MuSK-IgG levels measured by flow cytometry and RIA titers was found (r s = 0.74, 95% CI 0.41–0.89, p = 0.0003), as well as a moderate correlation between CBA end-point titers and RIA titers (r s = 0.47, 95% CI 0.01–0.77, p = 0.0414). A significant correlation was found between MuSK-IgG flow cytometry levels and disease severity (r s = 0.39, 95% CI 0.06–0.64, p = 0.0175; mixed-effects model estimate: 2.296e-06, std. error: 1.024e-06, t = 2.243, p = 0.032). In individual patients, clinical improvement was associated with decrease in MuSK-IgG levels, as measured by either flow cytometry or CBA end-point titration. In all samples, MuSK-IgG4 was the most frequent isotype (mean ± SD: 90.95% ± 13.89). A significant reduction of MuSK-IgG4 and, to a lesser extent, of MuSK-IgG2, was seen in patients with favorable clinical outcomes. A similar trend was confirmed in the subgroup of rituximab-treated patients. In a single patient, MuSK-IgG affinity increased during symptom exacerbation ( K D values: 62 nM vs 0.6 nM) while total MuSK-IgG and IgG4 levels remained stable, suggesting that affinity maturation may be a driver of clinical worsening. Discussion Our data support the quantification of MuSK antibodies by flow cytometry. Through a multimodal investigational approach, we showed that total MuSK-IgG levels, MuSK-IgG4 and MuSK-IgG2 levels, and MuSK-IgG affinity may represent promising biomarkers of disease outcomes in MuSK-MG.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study retrospectively investigated MuSK-IgG levels, subclasses (IgG4, IgG2, IgG1), and antibody affinity as biomarkers for severity and outcomes in a longitudinal cohort of 20 MuSK Myasthenia Gravis (MuSK-MG) patients. Findings indicate that lower total MuSK-IgG, MuSK-IgG4, and MuSK-IgG2 levels, along with lower MuSK-IgG end-point titers, are associated with clinical improvement and favorable treatment response. Conversely, increased MuSK-IgG affinity may drive clinical worsening. These markers correlate with disease severity and show promise for guiding treatment strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Rituximab and general immunosuppressive therapies for MuSK Myasthenia Gravis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Rituximab was administered to 9 out of 20 (45%) patients, with a median administration time of 10 years after disease onset. Specific dose, intensity, duration, or dose-response comparisons for rituximab or other immunosuppressive treatments were not detailed. Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIg) was not administered to any patient due to known poor response in MuSK-MG.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein Level (measured by Flow Cytometry (FACS), CBA titration, RIA, and ELISA, quantified as ABC values)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower levels (median: 59,853, IQR: 47,826–94,533) were associated with MM-or-better status compared to acute symptomatic phase (median: 116,889, IQR: 65,478–18,034) (p = 0.0295). Higher levels correlated significantly with MGFA clinical classification (r s = 0.3885, 95% CI 0.06383–0.6387, p = 0.0175). A trend toward reduction (median ABC differences: -107,000, -65%; p = 0.0625) was observed in RTX-treated patients with good clinical outcomes.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Pathogenic autoantibody targeting muscle-specific kinase (MuSK), critically involved in MuSK-Myasthenia Gravis pathogenesis by impairing neuromuscular junction function.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: MuSK-MG clinical status (severity, acute symptomatic phase, MM-or-better status, remission) and response to therapeutic intervention (including Rituximab).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A valuable biomarker for diagnosing, monitoring disease severity, and predicting clinical outcomes (improvement/worsening) in MuSK-MG. Lower levels are associated with better clinical status and favorable response to treatment, while higher levels indicate worse clinical classification. Potentially useful for guiding immunotherapy.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Antibody Titer (measured by live Cell-Based Assay (CBA))

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Median titers decreased from 1:400 in acute symptomatic phase to 1:200 with MM-or-better status (p = 0.0156). A trend toward reduction (1:100 vs 1:400, p = 0.0625) was seen in RTX-treated patients. In some cases, titers increased (e.g., 1:400 to 1:800) during remission or remained unchanged (1:800) during exacerbation. No significant correlation with MGFA clinical classification (r s = 0.2304, p = 0.1701).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Pathogenic autoantibody in MuSK-Myasthenia Gravis, reflecting the concentration of antibodies targeting muscle-specific kinase.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: MuSK-MG clinical status (acute symptomatic phase, MM-or-better status, remission, exacerbation) and response to treatment (including Rituximab).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as an indicator of clinical improvement in MuSK-MG, with lower titers associated with better outcomes. Used in diagnosis and monitoring, though showing weak correlation with clinical severity.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein Level (measured by flow cytometry, quantified as ABC values)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Most frequent isotype (mean ± SD: 90.95% ± 13.89). Showed a significant positive correlation with MGFA scores (r s = 0.3808, 95% CI 0.05487–0.6334, p = 0.0201). Significant reduction (median ABC differences: -47,438; p = 0.0245) in MM-or-better status. A trend toward reduction (median ABC differences: -4,652, p = 0.0625) was observed in RTX-treated responders. Levels remained stable in non-improving patients and during exacerbation in one case (90.8% and 81.3%).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Dominant pathogenic autoantibody subclass in MuSK-Myasthenia Gravis, primarily associated with MuSK-MG and produced by short-lived plasma cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: MuSK-MG clinical status (severity, acute symptomatic phase, MM-or-better status, remission, exacerbation) and response to conventional and Rituximab treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A valuable biomarker for disease severity and outcomes in MuSK-MG. Higher levels correlate with worse disease severity, while reduction is associated with favorable treatment response and good clinical outcome. Potentially supports immunotherapy tapering/suspension.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein Level (measured by flow cytometry, quantified as ABC values)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Represented 3.27% ± 3.98 of MuSK antibodies. Showed a significant reduction (median ABC differences: -2,303; p = 0.0085) in MM-or-better status, and a trend toward reduction (median ABC differences: -105,683, p = 0.0625) in RTX-treated responders. No significant changes in non-improving patients. No significant correlations with disease severity were found.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Pathogenic autoantibody subclass in MuSK-Myasthenia Gravis, contributing to the autoimmune response.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: MuSK-MG clinical status (MM-or-better status) and response to conventional and Rituximab treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduction is associated with favorable treatment response. Warrants further investigation for its clinical usefulness as a biomarker for MuSK-MG.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Median K D was 1.625 nM (range: 0.04 nM–61.9 nM). A 100-fold increase was observed during symptom exacerbation in one patient (K D values: 62 nM vs 0.6 nM), while it remained substantially unchanged (K D 1.3 nM vs 2 nM) when achieving MM-or-better status in another patient.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: The binding strength of autoantibodies to MuSK, which is a key determinant of their pathogenic potential and disease activity.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: MuSK-MG clinical status (symptom exacerbation, MM-or-better status), particularly in patients not receiving immunosuppressive treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased affinity may be a driver of clinical worsening in MuSK-MG, offering deeper insights into the immunobiology of the disorder and serving as a potential novel serologic biomarker of clinical outcomes.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein Level (measured by flow cytometry, quantified as ABC values)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Least frequent subclass, representing 2.47% ± 13.04 of MuSK antibodies. In one patient, levels switched from 2.76% in acute phase to 85.45% in pharmacologic remission. No significant correlations with disease severity were found.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Autoantibody subclass, potentially involved in immunobiological mechanisms driving clinical remission via IgG class switch.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: MuSK-MG clinical status (acute phase to pharmacologic remission), particularly in the context of IgG class switch.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: May suggest clinical remission is driven by IgG1+ B cell differentiation/recruitment in some patients, requiring further investigation as a biomarker for clinical outcomes.
